Great spot, quiet, diverse menu
Mar 2025 • Couples
Artist Alley was very near the hotel we were staying at in Dalat. It is set back from the road, and although it has a neon sign on the street entrance, it is quite easy to miss. Being set back from the road, it is quiet. We were greeted and directed upstairs. It is decorated with paintings on the walls. We had both lunch and dinner there (3 visits, that is how much we liked it). The host understands and speaks English well, and they were able to cope perfectly with vegetarian and gluten free dietary requirements. There is a good selection of both Western and Vietnamese food. I particularly liked the spaghetti bolognaise (vegetarian), and their special smoothy is also worth checking out. We didn't get a chance to try any of the deserts. Top notch, highly recommended.

Great dining experience
Jan 2025 • Couples
Lovely restaurant, not difficult to find using Google Maps, even though it is up an alley – as the name suggests. Walls covered with paintings and other artwork, and the space itself has been designed and created by Bien, who waited our table and whose family prepare the meals. Unfortunately, drinks list did not include local beer, but did include a small range of Da Lat and foreign red wines.

Bien, is friendly and his English is very good - he had visited London. 

The restaurant is very clean, and tables, coverings and napkins upmarket (proper table linen!). Interestingly, many tables were set with knife, fork and spoon place settings - we weren’t offered chopsticks nor a rice bowl: the hemisphere of steamed rice plus accompanying vegetables was brought to us on a dining plate.

Food was pretty good though not outstanding – that’s the only reason I haven’t given a 5 rating.
